content.text:
Operator
Good morning. Welcome to Indra's Q1 2025 Results Presentation. I'll now hand the conference over to Mr. Ezequiel Nieto Baquera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Ezequiel Nieto Baquera
Head of Investor Relations, Indra Sistemas
Gracias. Buenos días. Hello, good morning, and welcome to the Results Presentation of Q1 2025. My name is Ezequiel Nieto Baquera. I am the Investor Relations Director. First, please allow me to refer you to this slide that shows the legal framework under which this presentation would be taken into account. I would like to introduce the different speakers here today. José Vicente de los Mozos, he is the CEO of Indra. Luis Abril, Director General of Minsait. And Miguel Forteza, Financial Director of Indra. José Vicente, you've got the floor.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Welcome, everybody, and welcome to the Results Presentation of Q1 2025 of the Indra Group. Q1 started strong, offering good financial results and important advancements in the business, all fostered by a favorable market environment that's accelerating the growth pace of the company. Starting with the financial aspects, I'd like to highlight the performance for Q1, which is perfectly well aligned with our annual objectives. The main magnitudes include, first, our backlog increased by 11% to EUR 8 billion, and also the projects awarded have increased by 17%. Revenues in Q1 grew by 4%, pushed mainly by a growth of 18% in defense. EBITDA and EBIT increased by 7% and 6%, respectively, year-over-year. Net profit in Q1 dropped by 3% due to higher financial costs and taxes.
Free cash flow increased by 14% year on year, EUR 77 million compared to EUR 68 million in Q1 2024. The position of our cash flow in March 2025 was EUR 129 million compared to a net debt of EUR 89 million in March 2024. The Indra Group once again restates its commitment with all the financial forecasts for 2025 and for the 2026 objectives that can be found in the strategic plan Leading the Future. Let's now talk about business highlights, and in this case, I would like to highlight the execution of our strategy, Leading the Future. That's going ahead as expected. As you know, in the Q1, we have had a change of our president, Ángel Escribano. Ángel Escribano helps us to keep on working to be able to achieve our objectives.
We have had important investments, and we are getting ready for the advanced growth that we expected to have in the next few years. Among the most relevant milestones, I'd like to highlight the approval of a new organizational chart with focus around product and programs to guarantee, at the same time, standardization and industrialization, the deployment of a new industrial plan to transform Indra into a company that's product and manufacturing-oriented. At the same time, we'll be able to accelerate its internationalization, the appointment of a new technology director, a new CTO to reinforce our technology leadership. We have signed an MOU with Rheinmetall to modernize the Leopard 2E tanks for the Spanish army. Also, the creation of IndraMind and artificial intelligence platform to automate critical operations. We will show their results.
We have also reached important investments when closing the operations of Hispasat and Hisdesat. That's projected to take place in Q4 2025. As I mentioned, our growth has been supported by important, well, a very good environment due to the increase of defense budgets in Spain and other European countries. In this context, we expect that at least our figures in defense 2025 will double compared to 2024. Of course, we will provide more detail of the financial impact of this increase of defense expenditure in the presentation of the results of the H1 of the year once the programs launched by the government of Spain that could be led by Indra are further explained.
If we go into slide number six, the Q1 2025 has been a great, good start of the year for Indra, aligned with the budget for the year that, as I mentioned in the previous slide, allows us to keep our financial objectives for 2025. Our backlog has increased by 11%. It has given us further stability and visibility for the future growth of our income. In this quarter, it's based on the growth of Minsait and ATM. Order intake has increased by 70% with a strong growth in all the different divisions, amongst which we can highlight mobility, ATM, and defense that showed double-digit growth. Income has grown by 4%, and all the different business areas have shown increases except mobility that was flat.
This growth has been impacted in Q1 due to a lower punctual contribution of the business of elections compared to the same period in 2024. Excluding this temporary effect that will be diluted throughout the exercise, total income would have had a growth of 7%. Beyond the growth of our income, we have also improved operational profitability. EBITDA margin has reached 10.7%, which has meant growth in absolute terms of 7%. EBIT margin grew up to 8.2%, which brings about a growth of 6% that would have been 21% excluding the business of elections.
This performance has been translated into a net result of EUR 59 million with a solid cash flow generation of EUR 77 million, which is 14% above budget. A cash flow generation in the Q1 2024, closing the first three months of 2025, sorry, with a net cash flow of EUR 129 million. As you can see, never go back. Each quarter, we just keep on going forward. If we take a look at the slide number seven, we can see, well, our sales in the Q1, and we have achieved a growth of 5% in local currency and 3% in organic growth. The positive impact of our acquisitions and organic growth have balanced out the negative effect of exchange rates.
I would like to highlight as well that today in the group, over 53% of the group's EBITDA comes from our aerospace and defense business, as we can see in the chart in the lower right-hand side of the slide. In terms of the, well, the next slide in the evolution of our workforce. In this slide, I'd like to mention that we have achieved a growth of 2% of our income by employee compared to 2024 and +1% compared to the end of last year, with an increase of our workforce of 5% compared to December 2024. We keep on incorporating the best talent of the market to our business units aligned with our strategic priority of our plan, Leading the Future.
We still measure productivity in our operations through different tools, but at the same time, we are getting ready for the programs that are about to come with new technologies, for our talent to be able to provide these programs, on time and with right quality. If we focus around the results of business by business, starting with defense, as you can see in slide number 10. Our defense business has a solid growth in terms of order intake. It has increased by 27% in this quarter, mainly due to the contract of radars in Germany, naval systems business, and the inorganic contribution of Dimas. On its side, revenues has grown by 18% in this quarter, thanks to the contribution of Eurofighter, space, and the airborne platform business.
Besides these double-digit growths, EBITDA margin reached 18% and EBIT margin 15%. Those are our referential values in the sector. In slide 11, in ATM, the important performance shown by order intake that has grown by over 40%, mainly due to the new contracts of the UK and Spain, as well as the expansion in the region of AMEA, Azerbaijan, United Arab Emirates, and Malaysia. I must highlight that in ATM, today, we have the most modern solution in its field globally, and it's due to the great growth, and that's what's causing the growth we are seeing every day. Sales have increased by 6%, and we've had double-digit growth both in the United States and Canada in iTEC, as well as in Europe with Germany, Poland, and Romania.
EBITDA margin is at 16%, while EBIT margin was above 13%. In terms of mobility, slide 12. If we take a look at its results, order intake has increased strongly 73%, thanks to the urban transportation management systems in Ireland and the toll systems in Colombia. Sales were stable, with increases both in Europe and Spain that were balanced out by the drop that we have found in America and AMEA. Margins on this side have improved substantially, consolidating the levels of 7% in our EBITDA margin and 4% in EBIT margin, thanks to the lower impact of problematic projects we had in the past and the fact that we have focused more on the profitability of this division within our strategic plan.
If we take a look at slide number 13 and we see Minsait's results, we are still expanding our portfolio, our backlog, order intake and revenues with a growth of 14%, 4%, and 1%, mainly due to energy, industry, and financial sectors. These advancements place us clearly in a referential position within the IT sector. We see that our competitors are dropping. That's not our case. We keep on growing, we keep on increasing. We're doing a great work. Well, revenue have been impacted slightly due to a lower contribution of the elections business in this quarter. Excluding that impact, sales would have seen a growth of 5%.
If we were to eliminate the exchange rate effect, sales in local currency excluding acquisitions would have had even more solid growth of 7%, which is a reference within this sector right now, given everything that's happening at the European level. The profitability of Minsait is still increasing and EBITDA margin grew from 7.5% to 7.9% and EBIT margin from 5.5% to 5.6%. If we go to slide number 14 now and see the revenues of Minsait by different areas, we can see that we have optimized this month with digital and solutions with an increase of 7% compared to Q1 2024, which accounts for 53% of our sales.
Within digital, the sectors that are growing most are cybersecurity, migration to the cloud, and artificial intelligence. If we take a look at the drill down of the order intake of Minsait, it has increased by 4% in Q1 of the year, mainly due to a growth of 15% in energy and manufacturing. In terms of our revenues, we have seen an increase of 1% in the quarter, highlighting the good behavior shown by financial services, that increased 6%, and energy and manufacturing that increased by 5%. As you can see, the results are aligned. We are respecting our guidelines and our strategic plan.
Before I give the floor to our financial director, I would like to review with you which are the strategic priorities we've got today. First, we keep on reinforcing our approach in defense and aerospace. Our actions in this sector will follow the roadmap, the structural roadmap that includes five priorities. First, to develop new products and improve the competitiveness of the products that are already in our portfolio. Second, accelerate the growth of new business lines that will give a response to emerging needs of our clients. Third, escalate our industrial capacity to be able to face the strong growth of demand by redefining our engineering and manufacturing footprint. Fourth, to reinforce our internationalization capacities to be able to compete more efficiently in global markets.
Fifth, to increase industrialization, standardization, and integration of supply chain with the objective to reduce manufacturing costs and shorten the delivery lead times. I must say about this, that this quarter we have optimized supply chain by reducing the number of suppliers. I must say that we are going to keep on working on the implementation of Indra Space, which includes the integration of Hispasat and Hisdesat. We expect to capture synergies as well as generate additional business with IRIS² as a key program to foster growth. Our third priority is to continue the transformation in advanced technologies. In this sense, first, we will keep on turning the business mix of Minsait towards more added value solutions as well as increasing operational efficiency. Second, we will consolidate the presence of Minsait in priority geographies.
Third, we will start working with IndraMind, increasing its global presence. This will allow us to reinforce our home markets by reinforcing our presence and activity in preferential countries where our clients are and where clients with more potential are present. Fifth, we will continue with our portfolio rotation strategy through M&A operations, selected M&A operation, to close gaps and reinforce the ambition of Indra in long term. Six, we are going to increase our investment in R&D with the deployment of critical technologies and fostering our innovation engine, which is Indraventures. I like to highlight that last week, the European Union with 19 R&D initiatives have nominated Indra as leader in 14 of those, which shows our bet on technology.
Last, we will keep on betting on critical talent by attracting and keeping the best professionals. To do so, we are going to add over 2,500 people with a very high added value to get ready for the programs that are going to take place. These priorities reflect our focus for the year and restate our commitment with the Leading the Future guidance. Having said that, I'd like to give the floor to our CFO, Miguel Forteza, to keep on detailing the data. Thank you.
Miguel Forteza
Financial Director, Indra Sistemas
Thank you very much, José Vicente. Let's continue taking a look at the most important financial aspects of the Q1. First, I'd like to highlight the solid evolution of free cash flow in the Q1. It reached EUR 77 million and grew by 14% compared to Q1 2024. That was also an important quarter. It's an excellent figure. If we compare it to the history of Q1, taking into account the sustainability of this quarter in Indra, this shows the great performance of the operational execution of our businesses and the fact that we are focusing on the generation of cash flow.
In slide 19, in terms of the evolution of working capital, I'd like to highlight the positive evolution of days of sale that were at -9 compared to -3 in the same period of the previous year, and that were at -7 at the end of 2024, which shows the continuous effort of the operational management on accounts payable and receivable, whose objective is to optimize the cash flow. This figure is explained by eight days less in accounts receivable and another eight days in accounts payable, which compensates year-on-year +10 days of inventory due to the increased activity in the different businesses, especially businesses of aerospace and defense. Now let's explain the positive evolution of our net financial debt in Q1.
In which we have closed with a position of EUR 129 million compared to EUR 86 million that we found at the end of 2024. Among the different components, I would like to highlight, first of all, the operational contribution with EUR 98 million, but also the important change in working capital with a positive contribution of EUR 11 million, which brings about an improvement of EUR 26 million compared to the same period last year. As a result of it all, the leverage ratio is at -0.2x net debt EBITDA, which is an improvement of 0.4 compared to March 2024, as we can see in slide number 21.
Last, in terms of the structure of our debt, I like to highlight that we have been able to reduce the cost of our gross debt down to 3.4% compared to 4.2% that we had at the end of 2024. Having done that, the average maturity of our debt is at 3.3 years, compared to 1.5 years reported in the same quarter last year. We have also finished the quarter with a cash position of EUR 781 million, compared to EUR 616 million in 2024. Having said that, this is the end of our presentation. I would like to start the Q&A session.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, the Q&A session starts now. If you wish to ask the question, please press star followed by five on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from the line of Nicolas David from ODDO BHF. Please go ahead.
Nicolas David
Senior Sell-Side Equity Research Analyst, Oddo BHF
Yes, good morning. Thank you for taking my question. I have two related to the defense business. My first one is regarding the margin development in defense, which was down year-over-year, despite what looked like a positive mix, given the lower contribution from FCAS and good contribution from Eurofighter. Could you come back on why margin was down year-over-year in Q1, and what should we expect in the coming quarter?
My second question is regarding your comments about doubling order intake in defense in 2025 as 2024. I know that you are going to describe a bit more the H1 results, but could you give us already a sense of the type of bookings you expect there, and meaning, do you expect bookings generating revenue pretty quickly or bookings related to long-term program? Very last one on re-outscoping. When do you think that Tess Defence will be consolidated? Thanks.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Well, the first question is if you can explain the margins, and then I'll explain the second one. Yes. In terms of margin, operational margin, in absolute terms, it has grown by 2.7% at a lower pace than revenues due to higher level of amortization of this quarter, EUR 30 million compared to EUR 27 million. The margin drops to 9.2%. EBIT margin improves up to 8.2% due to lower operational expenses that took place in the previous quarter. Without the effect of amortization, the margin would have been better.
In terms of the contribution of Eurofighter, an important growth of the of defense linked to well the prospects have increased fixed costs of the company and has a higher impact in Q1 when revenues haven't yet reached the levels that we of the rest of the year. However, as months go by, sorry, revenues will increase, and this effect will dilute progressively, which will bring about an improvement of margins in the following quarters. Talking about order intake, as you know, we have the ReArm program at European level, and the Spanish government has a EUR 10 billion program.
About the EUR 10 billion program here in Spain, well, we have internally carried out an exhaustive analysis of which are the programs that could be led by us and what we are doing. Well, we're working around two main axes. First, to develop our capacities by hiring and launching production lines to be ready when the moment comes because where we believe we can grow in defense systems, radars, electronic warfare, control systems, that those are areas in which we are referenced. In tests, we believe we can integrate some new programs as well. In anti-drone and other weapons and ammunition issues, or programs, we believe we could be able to lead some of those programs as well.
We believe that we are at least going to double these figures. We believe that, frankly, that's gonna be more than that. Until there's further details about the programs, we don't really want to make any statement. I can say that we have the ambition to receive a relevant part of those programs coming from the government of Spain, and also part of the European programs. On the question about the consolidation of Tess, I must mention that we haven't yet closed it, and we expect to do that in the very short term, and that's when the consolidation of Tess will start. Thank you.
Nicolas David
Senior Sell-Side Equity Research Analyst, Oddo BHF
Thank you very much.
Operator
The next question comes from the line of Carlos Treviño from Banco Santander. Please go ahead.
Carlos Treviño
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Banco Santander
[Foreign language] Hola.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Even this year. Thank you.
Carlos Treviño
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Banco Santander
[Foreign language] Respecto-
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Well, just for you to, you know, to see this, our turnover in the US last year was EUR 72 million, with all our orders were EUR 100 million. Basically mobility business, ATM and Minsait. Exchange rate is protected at 100%. In terms of tariffs, within mobility, 80%, that's software. It's developed in the US, only 20% is developed elsewhere in terms of manufacturing. We're looking for an alternative to be able to manufacture those in the US for tolls. In terms of air traffic management, you know, we bought a company in Kansas. That's where we will develop the orders coming from the US.
The impact for us is low, it's moderate, and we believe the impact of tariffs could mean EUR 3 to 4 million, not above that. In terms of their budget in defense, well, there are 31 programs. We have made an analysis of those 31 programs, and we know which are the programs in which we can be prime and which are the ones in which we cannot be prime. If all the programs which are in the manufacturing of helicopters and planes, clearly that's not us. Airbus has a very good position. When talking about building boats, clearly Navantia has a leading position. In terms of the rest, we believe that many of those, Indra should actually lead. If we truly want to be a tractor company of defense in our country.
It's not a matter of a wish. We have to prove it and be ready for it. In that sense, we are working already on it because we believe we can be able to support this program. The impact this year is going to be in terms of order intake because having all the orders for EUR 10 billion at the end of May, of course, the impact is gonna be low. That's gonna have an impact in the budget for next year. We need to get the company ready, not for to reach an all-time high, but actually to achieve sustainable growth.
That growth is based on reinforcing engineering, reinforcing M&A that will provide us with better technology, have more vertical integration, developing products, be able to create or to sell or market those products globally. There's a lot of work that's going to help this growth. I mean, it won't have huge impact in sales in 2025, but it will have a huge impact in the following years. That's why beyond the EUR 6 billion that we have committed to in Leading the Future, we should start working to see when we're going to reach those. That's when we'll reach this EUR 10 billion. Thank you.
Carlos Treviño
Executive Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Banco Santander
Okay. Gracias.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Thank you.
Operator
The next question comes from the line of Michael Briest from UBS. Please go ahead.
Michael Briest
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Good morning. Two or three from me. Firstly, on the elections business, can you talk about how the rest of the year will pan out and give us a baseline for 2024? On Minsait, you talked about priority geographies, consolidating your presence there. Are you talking about M&A potentially, and in which markets that applies to? Just finally, obviously there was speculation in the press about an acquisition of Escribano Mechanical & Engineering. You said that there's no decision as of today. Can you talk about the process and obviously the shareholding structure and your chairman's ties to the company? How would that be managed internally from a sort of due diligence or compliance fashion given his shareholdings in both companies? Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Start by explaining the elections business and priority geographies and M&A and Minsait, and then I will tackle the question that all of you are waiting for, which is how are we going to tackle the Escribano project. Yes. Thank you very much, Michael. I can start by answering the first two questions. In terms of elections, the precise data on the Q1. In Q1 2025, the elections are EUR 9 million in sales. In Q1 2024, elections had the sales of EUR 36 million. So those are the figures for the Q1. In terms of our forecast for the end of the year, we expect the 2025 to be very close to 2024 in terms of election business, and it should be around EUR 55 to 60 million in sales. Those are sales.
In the elections business, you know that the margins are a bit above average. I believe that the initial effect of Q1 in total sales of Minsait, the impact it has had in the results shouldn't dilute throughout the year. In terms of the second question, you know that we, for some time, and that's part of Minsait strategy, we have focused around just a few geographies because our thought is that in the IT business scale is important. Not just global scale, but also local scale. The geographies in which we are present, well, besides Spain, Italy, and Portugal in Europe and a few more in the Americas, you know, those are important for us. The main ones are Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, and a few others.
The geographic criteria and keep on consolidating local scale is one of the criteria that we are taking into account to define our M&A strategy. Not only the geography, there's probably more important criteria that is linked to finding capacities that can complement the present portfolio of products and services, and digital capacities we have today. We are assessing this constantly. We have a constant pipeline of acquisitions that should fill this capacity gap map. We take a look on geographies, but also data, cyber, AI and so on. In terms of after what Luis Abril just mentioned, our M&A axis within the Leading the Future plan, I mean, it's also there for the rest of the areas of the company, not just Minsait.
What we do is to analyze which are the companies that can help us fill the gap in terms of technology or have a better integration of our supply chain or our value chain. Minsait, for example, a few months ago announced MQA, while also in terms of the avionics we have just mentioned. We are looking at other companies because if we want to be a tractor company in Spain, a relevant company here in Spain, we must analyze the different companies that can add value to Indra. Escribano is one of them. 25 April, we informed the CNMV, the Spanish SEC. Besides that, last week, I asked the board of Indra to inform of the fact that we are assessing other options. Why?
Because in this case, of course, there's a conflict of interest because the president of Indra is Ángel Escribano, and a member of the board is also Mr. Escribano, I mean, they've been out of the board, and I explained to the board where we are. We are in a very initial phase. Indra has not hired KPMG as we have seen in the press. We are carrying out an analysis, and I asked the board and the vice president of the board to be able to have a fluid relationship and to be able to see this operation so we are able to respect all the corporate governance rules, because we know how sensitive these operations could be. What can Escribano contribute with? Well, it can contribute with several aspects.
First, in terms of UAVs. I mean, we can do things like the ones we're doing. In terms of land vehicles, if we were to carry out this operation, can help us have further vertical integration and add value. At a point in which we need to develop our manufacturing capacities. Indra is a company with a huge history of engineering. But if I am allowed to say this, coming from my past experience in manufacturing in the automotive sector, it is a company that needs to get developed at an industrial level. We have to go from prototypes to serial manufacturing, and that can be provided by Escribano. Having said that, we are in an initial phase, just like another 20 companies I could mention in the Spanish and European scenario.
For the moment being, we have no valuation. As we go forward, and as soon as we have informed the board, as soon as there's relevant information, we will inform the CNMV, and we'll keep on going forward with this project, which is just one amongst many others. I am aware that in this case, I'm aware of the context in which this operation could take place. I hope this explanation was clear, and I hope there are no more doubts about it. Thank you.
Michael Briest
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, UBS
Thank you.
Operator
The next question comes from the line of Bruno Peça from CaixaBank. Please go ahead.
Bruno Peça
Equity Research Analyst, CaixaBank
Yes. Good morning, everyone. A few questions from my side. The first one on the evolution of the EBIT margin, particularly in the defense business in Q1, the decline that we saw on a year-on-year basis. If you could just explain a bit more the reason behind this decline and your expectations about the evolution towards the end of the year. This will be the first question. The second question more focused on your long-term outlook and strategic plan and targets. You mentioned that you expect to reach the targets before 2030. Two questions on this front.
The first one, if you believe that for reaching that target you will have to undertake more M&A, or if you could be close to that, at least close to that target only with the growth that your organic activity could have over the coming years. Second, also about this, what will be your expected level of leverage, net debt to EBITDA, when you reach those targets in terms of sales that you are foreseeing in your capital market, in your strategic plan. Thank you very much.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
I'll start with the first question about margin. Well, the growth we've seen in defense linked to our forecast have provided an increase of fixed costs on the company. We have to hire people, we have to get ready for these programs because, I mean, that's something that cannot be done overnight. Of course, this has had an impact in Q1, an impact that is under control when revenues haven't yet reached the levels for the rest of the year. For example, we have a rate of manufacturing backlog of three years.
Quite clearly that has to go down to one year or one year and a half, so we don't lose lead time opportunities, because one of the programs or one of the objectives in defense program is time delivery. That's why it is very important to be ahead of what's about to happen. Of course, that has an impact in fixed cost. But as the year goes by, revenues will increase and this effect will reduce. This is going to bring about an improvement of margins in the next few months. I have no doubt about it. We will finish the year with margins that will be similar to the margins including our guidance. I'm not concerned about it. We are just anticipating for what could happen.
Well, in terms of long term, the world has changed in the past seven months. On 6 March, we presented our Leading the Future plan. I see the plan. I mean, I'm not gonna say that's obsolete, but I. It needs to be refurbished because, well, we have a problem that's EUR 800 billion in the European Union, EUR 10 billion just this year in Spain. The context is different. Geopolitical scenario is different. Indra has to adapt to the new geopolitical context. That's why. I mean, we have to build with proper foundations. In 2025, don't be concerned. I mean, we're going to cover the financial guidance and expect to have even better results as we have done since I got here.
In the Leading the Future plan, I mean, the EBITDA and cash flow figures, I mean, we're gonna get there. We are already working beyond that. Those EUR 10 billion seem utopia when I. We see that that's not utopia anymore. That ambition has to. We have to work for that ambition. Well, we want to have a new capital market day to provide a long-term view. That's when we will be able to answer these questions you're asking. Which debt, which leverage ratio. I cannot give you that information today because we are still focusing around the short to midterm with the programs that are arriving. We are seeing how to reach those EUR 10 billion.
If at a certain point in time we need to go beyond a ratio of 1x, we'll do so because the context in this year or next year, it's not the same context we had some years ago. What's actually important today is that Indra has optimal financial debt position. Now that we are generating cash, our intake is over EUR 8 billion, our order intake is over EUR 8 billion. We're growing not just in defense, we're growing in ATM, in air traffic management at double-digit. We have the most advanced solution within mobility. We have carried out our restructuring. In Minsait, the work it's doing is just, it's outstanding. When our competitors are having issues to meet their budgets, we keep on growing.
We're working more and more to support this idea of being both military and civilian in all divisions. Long term view, of course we've got EUR 10 billion. Sure. When? Let's wait till things are a bit clearer and let's give an opportunity for the president to share that view when the time is right. We're working on this internal discipline. Never go back. Just keep on going forward. Every quarter, we keep on going forward. We're getting ready and preparing the company to have a great company in the future that was half asleep. It's awakening now, and we see this every day with the new results and more growth. In the defense sector, we want to be the tractor company at the national level, and we want to be a European reference with other companies in the sector.
Operator
The next question comes from the line of David López from JB Capital. Please go ahead.
David López
Director of Equity Research, JB Capital
Yes. Hi, good morning. My question is regarding the current status of the Minsait Payments divestment process. Is the transaction still ongoing? Should we expect it to close in the near term? Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra Sistemas
Well, the project is still open. If we find an interesting operation, we will carry it out. Otherwise, we won't. I believe the situation of the company is not forcing us to sell our payment methods, and we believe it adds value. I mean, it's part of our non-core business and just like Minsait, we have decided not to sell it, and we are working to try to keep on adding value to it, changing our mix. In that sense, as soon as there's more information on investment or divestment, we will inform you. In terms of payment methods, well, we'll wait, and we are still in the process. Well, there are no more questions.
I'd like to close the session, but first of all, I'd like to thank you for your support, your comments, and your trust in Indra Group, as we see every day, and we see the stock price. Please don't hesitate on the fact that we know what we're doing. We are going to meet our guidances, but we are getting Indra Group ready to become a reference company in Spain, in Europe, and we will keep on growing. Besides the first part of Leading the Future, we are already working towards this ambition to get to EUR 10 billion at some point, to be a profitable company and a reference company in Europe. Thank you.

content.text:
Ezequiel Nieto
Head of Investor Relations, Indra
Good morning, and welcome to our 2024 H1 Results Presentation. I'm Ezequiel Nieto, Head of Investor Relations, and as usual, let me refer you to disclaimer on slide number three that shows the legal framework under which this presentation must be considered. First, let me introduce the participants of this call. Marc Murtra, Executive Chairman of Indra, José Vicente de los Mozos, CEO of Indra, Antonio Mora, Chief Control Officer, and Luis Abril, Managing Director of Minsait. Marc, the floor is yours.
Marc Murtra
Executive Chairman, Indra
Thank you, Ezequiel. Good morning to everybody. Welcome to this conference call, in which we are pleased to present our results for H1 of 2024. I extend my thanks to all of you for your attendance. It is an honor for me to address you today in my capacity as Indra's Executive Chairman. The H1 of 2024 has been important for Indra, focused on setting us on the right implementation of our new strategic plan for 2024–2026, Leading the Future, unveiled in March of this year. That is our focus, execution. As defined in our strategic plan, Indra's vision is to become the Spanish multinational of reference in defense and aerospace and advanced digital technologies.
Over the last three months since the announcement of the plan, we have seen good progress, acting as a driver to build a path that will meet our Leading the Future strategic plan targets. Our double-digit growth in revenues, EBITDA, net income, and free cash flow compared to the H1 of 2023 is, in our view, a good headline of our performance. Our increased operational profitability, evidenced by improved EBIT and EBITDA margins, demonstrate the impact of the actions and initiatives we have executed over the past months, some of which we will discuss today. The financial performance is a testament to the work we have made in each of Indra's businesses. In our efforts to develop a defense ecosystem around Indra, we follow a collaboration and cooperation strategy with stakeholders in the sector.
As part of it, Indra invested in ITP in Q3 2023, and has now received a EUR 59.6 million dividend payment, representing the first returns on its investments. Please remember, ITP is not a financial investment for us, it is an industrial investment, but it has given us a good first return. In Air Traffic Management, we're focused on maintaining our leadership position in Europe, Middle East, and Latin America, ultimately aiming to become the number one player globally, reinforcing our position in North America and Asia Pacific. We are making progress in these new priority geographies, North America and Asia Pacific, leveraging key collaborations to access major renovation programs. In Minsait, we are working hard to evolve towards a digitally-focused portfolio, integrating capabilities in artificial intelligence, cloud, cybersecurity, and other high potential technologies to establish an industry-leading offering.
In fact, digital and solutions joint sales accounted for 50% of Minsait sales. Integration of mobility into Minsait, as laid out in our strategic plan, is set to further drive our digital-focused offering. Also worth highlighting are the advancements made over the last months in our technology roadmap. We are immersed in a process to identify the key future technologies, capabilities, and productions in which to invest. This initiative builds upon previous tech developments Indra has been working on, and its progress until 2030 will be closely monitored by a tech control tower. We're strengthening our organization with new appointments. We have recently appointed Miguel Forteza Garau, formerly Deputy CFO and Investment Director of the Nortia Group, as our new Chief Financial Officer, also joining Indra's executive committee.
Additionally, we are launching a new geographical organization, which our CEO will detail later on, resulting in the appointment of new regional directors. Latin America and Southern Europe will be led by Pedro Rodríguez Veiga, previously in charge of Minsait's international business. Middle East will be headed by Luis Permuy Muñoz-Rivero, who has been responsible for Indra's business in Asia, the Middle East, and Africa since 2016. United States, United Kingdom, and Northern Europe will be overseen by José Jacinto Monge Bravo, who joins the Indra Group. The rest of the world will be coordinated in an export model by José Luis Gascó, formerly responsible for the Asia-Pacific region. Thank you for your attendance and attention. I will now give the floor to our CEO, José Vicente de los Mozos.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Thank you, Marc. Good morning, everybody, and welcome to our H1 2024 conference call, and thank you for being with us here this morning. Let me begin by providing you all with Indra's main headline for the H1 2024. In terms of financial headline, these results are a clear sign of a successful kickoff of the implementation of a strategic plan. Our revenues, EBITDA, net income, and free cash flow in H1 2024 continued to grow at double-digit rate. Backlog and order intake grew by 5% and 7% respectively, showing our strong ability to generate business. This strong growth is accompanied by improvement in operating profitability, proved by increased EBITDA and EBIT margin across all our businesses.

Which is probably a sign of this message, you know, about our confidence in future growth. You know, because as I was saying, I mean, all verticals and most geographies are growing. We have good prospects for Europe, but also for other geographies. You said, I mean, can you-
Laurent Daure
Analyst, Kepler
The last question was on SAP.
Luis Abril
Managing Director of Minsait, Indra
You know, SAP, we see good prospects as well for SAP in the next, at least two, three years. I think that SAP is doing things well. I mean, all this movement to HANA and, you know, with the RISE initiative, I think that it is showing good demand from customers. We are well-positioned, I think, there, at least in some geographies and in some segments. As you know, we have something like 2,000 SAP consultants. You know, and as I was saying, we expect good growth. This should be one of the digital offering lines that should help us keep on growing, not only in this H2 2024, but probably in 2025 and 2026.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Okay. I want to thank-
Laurent Daure
Analyst, Kepler
Okay, thank you so much.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
I want to thank everybody today for participating and listening to us. Leading the Future is on track. As I told before, some doubt about implementation. Leading the Future will be implemented at the right time with the right performance. Indra is growing in all the divisions. I want to take this opportunity to thank all the employees in Indra and all the board's support for us, and also the president for the confidence because Indra is back. Thank you.
Marc Murtra
Executive Chairman, Indra
Thank you, José Vicente. Thank you, everybody. Good August. Goodbye. Bye.

content.text:
Operator
Results presentation. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ezequiel Nieto, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Ezequiel Nieto Baquera
Head of Investor Relations, Indra
Thank you. Good morning, and welcome to our Q1 2024 Results Presentation. I'm Ezequiel Nieto, head of investor relations, and as usual, let me refer you to the disclaimer on slide number three that shows the legal framework under which this presentation must be considered. First, let me introduce the participants of this call: José Vicente de los Mozos, CEO of Indra, Antonio Mora, Chief Control Officer, and Luis Abril, Managing Director of Minsait. José Vicente, the floor is yours.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Thank you, Ezequiel. Ladies and gentlemen, good morning, and welcome to our conference, and thanks for being with us this morning. I think it's fair to say that our Q1 results have been very strong and positive. They are a great starting point for our strategic plan Leading the Future and the right first step to achieve its target. Let's start with the slide number five, where we display our main business achievement for the quarter. First of all, we have taken our first step to deliver on our strategy presented in the Capital Markets Day by creating our space subsidiary with the aim of making it the cornerstone of our business activity in the coming years. As we said, we are committed to becoming a tier-one European player in space.
We have also carried out the acquisition of the whole capital of Global Training Aviation to reinforce our position as one of the world's leading simulation company. With this operation, Indra now covers the entire value chain of the business, from the manufacture of leading edge simulator to the provision of training services for pilots. Another very important milestone has been the joining of NAV CANADA into the iTEC Alliance, where Indra is a major player in the global air traffic ecosystem. With this important partnership, iTEC has reached beyond the European border for the first time. We have also signed several agreements with top players of defense industry, such as the next generation radar in United Arab Emirates with EDGE Group, the new industrial collaboration agreement signed with Lockheed Martin, or the collaboration agreement signed with Thales to boost the joint development and commercialization of vanguard defense system.
Finally, we have achieved two new relevant milestones in ESG, which are the best score in the technology sector in the S&P yearbook and the renewal of our Top Employer certification for the sixth consecutive year as one of the best companies to work for. On page six, we can see the headline of our financial results for Q1 2024. Just let me highlight the following. First, the double-digit growth achieved in the order intake, revenue, EBIT, and EPS. Second, the size and quality of our backlog, which grew 6.3%, providing good visibility for our near future growth. Third, the commercial momentum that the company is going through, with revenues growing at a 22% rate, strongly backed by all our divisions, among which stands out the growth registered by Defence, +56%, and ATM +63%.
Besides that, this growth, combined with our cost measure, are driving our improvement in profitability, as our EBITDA and EBIT margin show, and cash generation, allowing us to maintain financial leverage at a very low level of just 0.2x. On slide seven, just let me remark the strength of our organic growth, 90% +1, remove the Forex impact and inorganic contribution. In terms of EBITDA distribution, Defence, Air Traffic Management, and Mobility represent 53% of the total for Q1 of the year. On page 8, we display the evolution of our headcount. Let me highlight here that we have improved our revenue per employee by 14%, while our workforce has only increased by 2% compared to March 2023. The productivity become also a key element in our performance.
Now, once the big picture has been presented, let's dive into the performance of each of our four divisions, starting in page 10 with Defence. In slide 10, this has been a very strong quarter for Defence, as you can see in the key figures on the slide. Order intake grew by 4%, mainly due to the Eurofighter project and despite the worse FCAS project comparable. More important are the very strong sales figures, which grew 56% in Q1 2024, mostly driven by the contribution of the FCAS project. Excluding this contribution, sales would have increased by 10%. On top of this solid revenue growth, EBIT margin grew from 15.7% last year same quarter to 16.4% in Q1 2024. Improvement explained by the increasing contribution of the FCAS project.
In Air Traffic Management we also deliver very strong performance, as you can see on slide number 11. The positive performance shown by order intake +83% growth was mainly due to the contracts signed in Canada and Colombia, as well as some other in Europe and EMEA. It is worth noting, as we mentioned before, that NAV CANADA joined the iTEC Alliance. Sales in Q1 2024 grew by +63%, driven mainly by contracts carried out in Belgium and Spain, as well as the inorganic growth from the acquisition of Park Air in the UK and the Selex business in the US. Finally, EBIT margin was in the double digits range of 13.8%.
If we move to the Mobility division, backlog and order intake fell slightly, -3%, -1% respectively, although sales grew +19%, driven by double-digit growth in all geographies except for Spain. The EBIT margin in Q1 2024 was 3.2%, slightly higher than 2.7% recorded in Q1 2023. Frankly, big jobs done deeply in mobility section to prepare for the future. About Minsait. Now on page 13, Minsait also presented a very positive quarter. The good commercial momentum goes on with a +7% increase in order intake in Q1 2024.
For its part, revenue in Q1 2024 grew by +12%, driven by the strong performance shown in public administration and healthcare, which grew +35% thanks to the positive activity with the public administration in Spain, while energy and industry posted +8% growth, and financial services registered a +3% increase. Finally, EBIT margin in Q1 2024 improved to 5.5% versus 5.1% in Q1 2023, thanks to higher operating leverage from the steady sales growth, as well as improved revenue mix and the further efficiency initiatives. When we compare the performance of Minsait, you can see the good job done in Q1 2024 for the team.
On page fourteen, the breakdown of Minsait revenue by horizontal, where you can see that we have improved our mix with digital and solution growing by 15% compared to Q1 2023 and now representing 50% of our sales. Finally, on page fifteen, we saw our order intake and revenue breakdown of Minsait. Q1 2024 order intake was up 7%, with double-digit growth in three of the vertical, except for energy and industry, which declined by -8%. On the right-hand side, revenue in Q1 2024 grew by +12%, driven by public administration and healthcare for +35%, energy and industry +8%, and financial services +3%. On the contrary, revenue in telecom and media decreased -4%. Now I leave the floor to Antonio Mora for the financial review.
Antonio Mora
Chief Control Officer, Indra
Thank you, José Vicente. Good morning, everyone. Let's start the financial review with the evolution of the free cash flow on slide 17. That amounted to EUR 68 million, an excellent figure taking into account business seasonality and considering that we are more than doubling the already good figure for the same quarter last year. This level of cash generation, as we will see below, has allowed us to maintain our financial leverage in a very low level. Now in page 18, we see how days of sale improved compared to both March 2023 and the end of last year. The good performance versus March 2023 can be explained by the improvement of accounts receivable, -2 days, and accounts payable, -5 days. Page 19 shows the net debt evolution of the quarter.
The first step is strong operating cash flow of EUR 108 million due to the excellent performance of the business. As mentioned, net working capital stood at EUR -15 million, well below the EUR -34 million posted in Q1 2023. Other financial liabilities stood at EUR 9 million, similar figure as the previous year, and net interest at EUR 4 million, slightly higher than Q1 2023. With all this, we have closed this first quarter with net debt at EUR 89 million and a leverage ratio of 0.2 net debt to EBITDA, as you can see in page 20. Slightly above the figure we presented in March 2023, but still at very low debt levels. Now, to finish my speech, a quick look to the capital structure in page 21.
In Q1 2024, gross debt remains stable at EUR 697 million. Average maturity below two years and cost of debt at 4.2%. The cash position at the end of March was EUR 608 million, and we also have EUR 748 million of undrawn credit facilities, so that we maintain liquidity while canceling gross debt with cash. Now let me turn the call to José Vicente for the final slide.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Well, as you can see, that's the beginning, our strategic plan Leading the Future. We resolve. First, I want to congratulate the team. I think this transformation of Indra, we start to see the result. I am very proud of my team. We are working very solidly, and as you can see the speed of the transformation. This month we'll launch Capital Markets Day, but we don't sleep. Now, I want to show you the eight workstreams to implement Leading the Future. As we advance our Vision 2024/2026 Strategic Plan, Leading the Future, I'm eager to present to you how we have structured the implementation around eight critical workstreams.
The first workstream, our control tower and operating model, is designed to oversee the overall status of the plan's implementation and to deploy key organizational and operating model changes, and it will be chaired by the chairman and myself. The transformation workstream is set to drive improvement across several fronts, accelerating our business top line, boosting industrial and software development productivities, and laying the groundwork for the newly announced Indra Technology Hub, expected in 2026. These initiatives are crucial for our growth and efficiency. The focus of the strategic corporate operation workstream is to oversee the creation of the Indra Space, including the carve-out of current capability and leading the search for global long-term partners and new companies to be incorporated. Additionally, this workstream will guide us in the portfolio rotation process, which includes the divestiture of non-core assets and acquisition of defense and aerospace target.
It will also lead the search for new key strategic partnerships and alliance. Our geographic expansion workstream aims to position Indra as a stronger multinational company, enhancing local positioning and customer proximity by deploying three new clusters or home markets, as announced in our Capital Markets Day. The group-wide digital capabilities workstream is focused on expanding midsize digital capabilities across the organization. The technological R&D workstream will prioritize investment in digital and cutting-edge technologies as part of our commitment to invest over EUR 3 billion in technology development up to 2030. Our corporate enabler workstream is tasked with supervising the implementation of our new talent plan, which includes the deployment of the new Indra Way culture and initiative in all the key areas such as ESG, branding, and digitalization of corporate systems. Lastly, the booster workstream is where we will explore additional opportunities to further accelerate Indra's growth.
If we go to the next slide, turning to the implementation phase of our strategic plan, we are currently in the activation period. Our focus is on making critical organizational adjustments and laying a robust foundation for all subsequent action. Since the Capital Markets Day, we have been structuring and planning meticulously all the subject. New committees have been established, and we are implementing advanced monitoring tool to ensure transparency and control. We have also kick-started priority action with dedicated sponsor. It's for that we have defined the first 100 days, that we have the action, that we have the responsible for each committee direction or inside the team with related data to be implemented. Looking ahead, we anticipate the rollout and execution phase of our strategic plan to commence by Q3 of this year.
This phase approach ensures that we are not only adequately prepared for the strategic plan launch, but also proceed in a manner that guarantees success. As you can see, first, we have defined the Chief Transformation Officer, that he will be responsible for monitoring, follow, support the team in its action. Also, we have defined the CTO to lead a strategic corporate transaction work team end-to-end. Control tower, I explained before, and a quick start with a +15 priority work stream to first 100 day with assigned sponsor. The immediate priority activity to define is new top management mid-term incentive scheme linked to guidance and release on Capital Markets Day that needs to be approved in the next shareholder and space new cooperative as part of Indra core priority.
I remind why we go to develop the space, because communication is part of those businesses. Countries need to be autonomous, they need to control the communication. It's for that makes sense, we develop this new space comm. That's all for Q1. We continue to work. Thank you all for being here today and for your time, and thank you to those that are making this plan a reality. I see you at the end of July. Thank you very much. Now we are open to the Q&A.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, the Q&A session starts now. If you wish to ask the question, please press star followed by five on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from the line of Nicolas David from Oddo BHF. Please go ahead.
Nicolas David
Branch Manage of Corporate and Markets Madrid, Oddo BHF
Yes. Good morning. Thank you for taking my question and congrats for this very impressive set of Q1 earnings. Just maybe talking about the outlook, in the press release, you just reiterate the annual guidance for this year. How should we read that? Should we read that as a way you expect a softer growth in the coming quarter or it's just your internal processes which makes you not to upgrade it while you see actually a better outlook than what is in your guidance? We understand that Q1 was probably the strongest quarter of the year, but not only because FCAS comps are going to be tougher going forward.
Could you please highlight some other potential exceptional item which pushed the growth in Q1 and we shouldn't see in the rest of the quarters, notably Air Traffic Management? How sustainable is the growth, the organic growth you have now, notably in those countries you mentioned, and when the big contracts you've signed in Canada and Colombia are going to ramp up? I have a second question: could you please update us on the process to dispose of a stake in Minsait, where it stands now? There were some rumors in the press that you are more open to sell a majority stake, and when should we expect an update on that official? Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Thank you, Nicholas. Well, okay, about your three questions. First one, about the guidance. Well, it's just one quarter, and we prefer to be conservative. Bear also in mind, we have the positive delta of FCAS EUR 56 million in the quarter. This delta disappear to the remaining quarters. I explained before, I don't want never go back. Okay? I think the key point is the split, the team to improve. This year is the first years to implement the plan. I think for the moment, I prefer to be conservative. About Air Traffic Management. Frankly, to put Air Traffic Management, that clear division has been very good input for all the customer and shareholder. Because before, Air Traffic Management does. I remember we are the second company in the world, and maybe we are the most advanced solution for the airports worldwide.
They put air traffic in relevance. I can tell you, for example, when I visit Geneva in the airspace exposition, that Indra today is a reference in this domain worldwide, that I'm very confident about air traffic management. Now, that we explain in the Capital Markets Day, for us, the key point is to enter the US market, that in the following years the airports will be renewed. Also, I can tell you in the last month, we have won a small project for more than 40 small airports for anti-drone planes in US. That's the beginning, that we are confident. About Minsait, frankly, after one year, if I listened to all the rumors, I never could work. Okay? We have taken commitment.
I think step by step, I'll explain to you, we have more than 50 answers in the 100 days. We are looking for a partner for Minsait. We are studying non-core business. It's time to be a little patient. We don't stop, but I think we have clear direction where we want to finish.
Nicolas David
Branch Manage of Corporate and Markets Madrid, Oddo BHF
Understood. On Minsait, beyond the rumors, I mean, is it true that you are just in the phase of receiving offers yet, or it's really too early in the process, yeah.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Please give us time. Okay? It's under control. Also, this project is led by Luis Abril, as you know, he's the head of Minsait division. We have the schedule, and we know how to do in the following months.
Nicolas David
Branch Manage of Corporate and Markets Madrid, Oddo BHF
All right. That's all. Given the very strong performance, we are happy to let you start. Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Next question, please.
Operator
The next question comes from the line of Laurent Daure from Kepler. Please go ahead.
Laurent Daure
Equity Analyst, Kepler
Yes, thank you. Good morning, gentlemen. Couple of questions from me as well, starting with Minsait. Could you give us an update on what you see on the market, on your key regions, Spain and LATAM, as you probably saw, most of your competitors are not growing anymore, and you're still delivering 10% organic growth. I know Spain has been more resilient, but do you see the first sign of weakness? More particularly, you were boosted by the public sector. Do you expect the same inflows of revenue from a large government contract for the rest of the year? That's the first point. The second question is on the Defence business. It's always very hard for us to forecast.
If you could give us your best guess for 2024 versus 2023 on this business. My final question is back to your good working capital control in Q1. I was wondering if the shift towards more defense business can have an impact going forward, not only this quarter, but for the next years on the speed of cash collection. In other words, the receivables. I think there's quite a difference between IT and defense. If you could clarify a little bit on that topic, that would be useful as well. Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Laurent, before to give the floor to Luis for Minsait, about the election. Election will spend lower contribution around EUR 55 to 60 million versus EUR 69 million 2020 to 2023, but we are in May. We don't know political overview in the following months. Maybe will be lower, maybe will be higher. Because you know, more and more we are invited to more RFQ to prepare election worldwide. Now, Luis will answer you about Minsait.
Luis Abril
Managing Director of Minsait, Indra
Thank you, José Vicente. Yes, I mean, just to complement on election shouldn't be, you know. This year shouldn't be very different from 2023. You know, 2022 was quite good for elections. 2023 and 2024 should be similar. On Minsait, you know, effectively, as you seen the numbers, we still see no significant signs of a slowdown. You know, it is true that in this quarter, the fastest growing vertical has been public administrations. In public administrations, you know, not only we do have the Spanish public administration, we have many other things. We have health, we have actually elections and some other things.
As you can see, you know, with the exception of telco and media, there is growth, what we consider solid growth in all the verticals. You know, overall, we see no signs of a slowdown. It is true that, you know, some of our peers have been more pessimistic in the last months, and actually some of them have been having some problems. It's not our case. You know, for the future, we are still cautiously optimistic. You know, we have a good pipeline. You know, we are seeing solid demand from our customers.
It is true that we probably do have some advantages versus our most relevant peers, such as the fact that most of our customers are large customers, who are suffering the crisis less, or the fact that many of our contracts are multi-annual contracts, you know, which give us some baseline, which is interesting from a growth perspective. You know, we are typically in very core activities of our customers. We are relatively confident with the fact that we can keep on growing. You know, it is true that public administration in this quarter has been relevant from a growth perspective.
You know, we keep on relying not only on public administration, but in all the sectors that compose Minsait, and as I was saying, we are cautiously optimistic. You know, still, given that we are cautious, what we see for this year, for the end of the year in Minsait is still, you know, growth figures of mid-single digit and no more. You know, we feel that we can comfortably fulfill that kind of figures.
Laurent Daure
Equity Analyst, Kepler
Okay. Thank you. The last point was on the working cap.
Luis Abril
Managing Director of Minsait, Indra
Yes. Regarding your question about the working capital, it will be better in Defense and ATM, thanks to the prepayments and the very good collection during Q1 2024.
Laurent Daure
Equity Analyst, Kepler
Okay. Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Next question, please.
Operator
The next question comes from the line of Carlos Iranzo from Bank of America. Please go ahead.
Carlos Iranzo Peris
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Hey, guys. Good morning. I actually have three questions. The first one on free cash flow: very strong quarter, your reiterated guidance. I just wonder how should we think about free cash flow generation in the next three quarters. Is 2024 a year in which you are not going to generate most of your free cash flow in Q4? Second question on Defence, 70 basis points of margin expansion at the EBIT level despite the strong contribution from FCAS. Just wondering if you can give a bit of color on the revenue mix and how have you been able to increase margins despite the strong contribution from FCAS.
Last one, if you can help me in terms of modeling on Air Traffic Management, could you please give us the inorganic contribution from Selex and Park Air, please? Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Carlos, first, before to give the floor to Antonio, answer you about the free cash flow and the contribution for Selex ES and Park Air. In Defense without Eurofighter and without FCAS. Okay? Defense, we have increased 10% without FCAS revenue. Okay? About the EBIT. Our EBIT margin in Defense has been 16.4% versus 15.7%, improving thanks to operating leverage and FCAS contribution. For example, I can explain to you, for example, cost reduction in manufacturing has been important. We are improving efficiency, and now we are forecast to establish the second shift in September. That this operational point also supporting us to improve our EBIT margin. Antonio.
Antonio Mora
Chief Control Officer, Indra
Okay. We reiterate our guidance of EUR 250 million for the full year in free cash flow. We'll hope the Q4 will be the stronger generation of free cash flow.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Carlos, your question
Carlos Iranzo Peris
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Very clear. On ATM and the inorganic contribution.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Selex ES and Park Air. Okay, yes.
Antonio Mora
Chief Control Officer, Indra
Okay, Carlos?
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Selex and Park Air.
Carlos Iranzo Peris
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Yes, Miguel.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
The contribution, Selex ES and Park Air has been EUR 9 million. For this Q1.
Carlos Iranzo Peris
Equity Research Analyst, Bank of America
Thank you.
Antonio Mora
Chief Control Officer, Indra
Thank you. Selex, EUR 7 million and EUR 2 million for Park Air. Next question.
Operator
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, please be reminded that in order to ask a question, you may press the star key followed by five on your telephone keypad. Our next question comes from the line of Michael Briest from UBS. Please go ahead.
Michael Briest
Managing Director and Head of European Technology Research, UBS
Yes, good morning. Congratulations as well from me on the strong start. On space, what's the significance of creating the stand-alone company? Can you make any comments on the press speculation regarding Hispasat? Secondly, on Minsait, the revenues are obviously strong, but headcount was flat year on year. Does that suggest a lot of the growth was, you know, products, subcontracting, maybe the election business? Because normally we'd see a stronger margin drop through if headcount was flat on that sort of growth rate. Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Space. When we have explained our concept in new space to the shareholder consultant, there has been very open interest because we have in mind a very agile space newCo that each company will have his autonomy, in some case we can buy also, but also to maximize the synergy and the same potential, sales strategy. That, today, for example, we are in the process to affiliate our communications group. We are in the discussion of different companies around the value chain that for the moment I cannot give you the name. Hispasat that I explained is an option, but it's not the only option. Okay? Because we want to become European partners. That Hispasat can be in the operator part of the newCo, yes. Can be other non-Spanish company, yes.
It depends on the following months that the discussions we have with different companies in Europe and also in some cases with US companies.
Luis Abril
Managing Director of Minsait, Indra
I take that one on myself. Michael, thank you for the question. You mentioned the headcount, which is constant. Effectively it is constant, despite the growth. This has to do not that much with extraordinary effects or peaks of things like the acquisition business. It has to do basically with the fact that sales are more high quality sales than before. We are selling more digital. We are selling more projects and services which are less intensive in people. We are selling less BPO and things like that. This allows us to grow without significantly increasing headcount.
Michael Briest
Managing Director and Head of European Technology Research, UBS
Wouldn't that create a bigger margin benefit? I know margins are up, but 10% growth without any headcount should have a bigger effect, I'd have thought.
Luis Abril
Managing Director of Minsait, Indra
Well, actually, if you take a look at operating margin and EBIT, the margin is better than in Q1 2023. It is actually significantly better. It's like four, five or six percentage points better.
Michael Briest
Managing Director and Head of European Technology Research, UBS
Okay, thank you.
Luis Abril
Managing Director of Minsait, Indra
Thank you. Any other questions?
Operator
There are no further questions at this time. Thank you.
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Okay, thank you, ladies and gentlemen, and I hope to see you at the end of Q1, say, at the end of Q2. Thank you. Have a nice day, nice week.

content.text:
Operator
Good morning and welcome to Indra's Q3 results presentation. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Ezequiel Nieto Baquera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Ezequiel Nieto Baquera
Head of Investor Relations, Indra
Good morning, everybody, and welcome to our presentation. Thank you everyone for joining us today, especially those of you who have been able to come here in person. I'm Ezequiel Nieto, Head of Investor Relations, and as usual, let me refer you to the disclaimer on slide number three that shows the legal framework under which this presentation must be considered. Now let me introduce the participants of this call. Marc Murtra, Chairman of Indra, José Vicente de los Mozos, CEO of Indra, Borja García-Alarcón, our CFO, and Luis Abril, our Managing Director of Minsait. Now let me turn the call to Marc Murtra, our Chairman. Marc, the floor is yours.
Marc Murtra
Chairman, Indra
Good morning, everybody, and welcome to our Q3 2023 results presentations. Before our CEO showcases our strong results, I would like to highlight some relevant contextual points. We're at a time of transformation and opportunities in our key markets. The world continues to change. Security events have dramatically accelerated the concern and focus on defense and security in the European Union and its allies. We expect defense spending to grow dramatically in the coming years. Strategic autonomy strongly emerges as a global trend. Air traffic recovery has been surprisingly swift after COVID, and we are now in 2019 traffic levels. Growth for 2024 is expected to be above 4%. Mobility's new paradigms are reaching maturity, such as pay-as-you-go service, free flow, or mobility as a service.
Technology has changed the playing field significantly with the growing demand for cybersecurity and generative artificial intelligence. Gen AI specifically has the potential to be a game changer. We are fully aware of and have internalized the disruptive changes that are on the horizon in the realm of technology. We are actively preparing to navigate this new era. Key changes are steady, underway, and we are strategically focusing on high-value, rapidly growing market segments. We continue with our transformation of our company. A previous strategic reflection unfolds as our new strategic plan, which will be well-timed, ambitious, and achievable.
Regarding corporate governance, we have established a new board executive committee with eight members, four of whom are independent to accelerate decision making. Finally, after reorganizing our key management team, we are now rolling out these changes to the downstream structure to ensure that they are implemented effectively. We believe that these changes will allow Indra to successfully navigate this era of uncertainties and opportunities to achieve its full potential of growth and value. Now, José Vicente will explain the results in detail. José Vicente?
José Vicente de los Mozos
CEO, Indra
Thank you, Mark. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome everyone to the war room of Leading the Future, the place where we are developing our strategic plan. We have summoned you to this specific place because we wanted you to experience the spheres where our team, from senior manager to the fresh talent, is defining Indra's future for the next 10 years. Let's move now to the slide number six, where we display the main Q3 results highlights. As you can see, the results for the first nine months of 2023 continue to be strongly positive, reaching a new all-time high in orders backlogs. CEO, Indra
Those final comments before our chairman closes out this session. First, I want to thank you, all you analysts, because in the different meetings I met you have been very confident with Indra, confident in my appointment. I told you Indra is very good company. The talent I met here is amazing. I think with Leading the Future, we can show a transformation in this company and become an actor in different worlds today. That is clear in IT with Minsait, we are referring. In air traffic, we are referring. In defense, we need to grow to become somebody in Europe. Mobility, we need to be focused in technological mobility. We know where we can go. I think your continuous feedback supports us, helps us to take the best decision.
Thank you, and I'll see you when we close out 2023. Bye.
Marc Murtra
Chairman, Indra
Yeah. I wanna thank José Vicente for bringing his tremendous energy to the company, and it's great working with him. Things, I think, are going very well. Also, Luis, for his ongoing and continuous wonderful work on the IT business, which you know is a tough business. It's not for everybody. We see the future with optimism. Of course, we have to deliver, we have to focus, we have to work hard, and there are always risks, but risks always comes with return. Thank you everybody, and thank you Borja and the team for organizing this.
